spots.bio: Jetty known for diving and snorkelling among seahorses, Port Jackson sharks and leafy sea dragons.
spots.name: Edithburgh Jetty
spots.note: Wikivoyage lists it as its own destination (dive site), and the tourism board says it is renowned for diving and snorkelling with seahorses, Port Jackson sharks and leafy sea dragons; a jetty walk and shore dive a visitor goes for.

spots.bio: 1882 lighthouse reserve at the peninsula's south-western corner, reached by Lighthouse Road.
spots.name: Corny Point Lighthouse
spots.note: Listed as an attraction by yorkepeninsula.com.au and southaustralia.com; an 1882 lighthouse reserve reached by Lighthouse Road with a picnic area and coast to linger on; Wikivoyage names it too. Free, self-guided.

spots.bio: Salt lakes on the Yorke Peninsula Salt Lake Trail, with a viewing platform at Pink Lake and a boardwalk at Par Lake.
spots.name: Yorketown Pink Lakes
spots.note: Tourism board and southaustralia.com name the Yorke Peninsula Salt Lake Trail (self-drive routes, boardwalk at Par Lake, Pink Lake viewing platform, 15 to 90 min). Objection: lake colour varies by season, and it could duplicate a Salt Lake Trail candidate.

spots.bio: Old port jetty and cliff-top lime kilns with a lookout on the coast road.
spots.name: Wool Bay Jetty and Lime Kilns
spots.note: Tourism board page names the uniquely designed lime kilns on the cliff top and the old port jetty, with a lookout; a free heritage stop on the coast road. Objection: a short stop, one source.

spots.bio: Western-coast town with an 1878 jetty, a maritime museum and a geology trail.
spots.name: Port Victoria
spots.note: Town with a historic 1878 jetty, Port Victoria Maritime Museum and geology trail; named by yorkepeninsula.com.au and southaustralia.com (rules 1, 2).

spots.bio: 1877 cargo shed by the jetty telling the story of the windjammer grain races.
spots.name: Port Victoria Maritime Museum
spots.note: Two sources: yorkepeninsula.com.au Port Victoria page and visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (1877 cargo shed by the jetty telling the windjammer grain-race story). Objection: open weekends 2-4 pm only.

spots.bio: Free display of the Red Devil monoplane that made the first airmail flight over the sea.
spots.name: Minlaton Harry Butler Red Devil Memorial
spots.note: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Minlaton and the yorkepeninsula.com.au Minlaton page (the only genuine Red Devil monoplane, first airmail over the sea, free display on the edge of town).

spots.bio: Seaside town on the east coast of the Yorke Peninsula with a beach and jetty.
spots.name: Port Vincent

spots.bio: 1876 jetty still used by fishers and white beaches on Hardwicke Bay, with boating and diving.
spots.name: Point Turton
spots.note: Tourism board page: 1876 jetty (still used by fishers), white beaches on Hardwicke Bay, boating and diving; a second-tier seaside stop. Beach and jetty are one place (Point Turton Beach is a duplicate).

spots.bio: Surf breaks and three swimming beaches, with a coastal drive from Corny Point to Berry Bay.
spots.name: Corny Point
spots.note: Tourism board page names surf breaks (Rock Pool, Salmon Hole, Daly Head, Berry Bay), three swimming beaches and the Corny Point to Berry Bay coastal drive; visitors beaches stop. Lighthouse is a separate candidate.

spots.bio: Safe white-sand beach with no rips, good for crabbing and swimming, beside Pine Point.
spots.name: Black Point
spots.note: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage (own section with Pine Point, "one of the most gorgeous stretches of coastline") and the tourism board page (safe white-sand beach with no rips, crabbing, swimming).

spots.bio: White-sand swimming beach south of Edithburgh, at the end of the mosaic walking trail.
spots.name: Sultana Point
spots.note: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Edithburgh Do names it as the swimming beach south of town with white sand and the end of the mosaic walking trail; a second-tier beach stop (COVERAGE.md).
